messages:
Leo: Quick summary of the geo+GPU sweep comparing real-time (SSE / WS) vs batched non-streaming endpoints. Pushed plots to the perf bucket: gs://redwood-perf/2265/rt_vs_batch/* and uploaded a few PNGs to the thread (rt_vs_batch_us-west-A100.png, rt_vs_batch_eu-central-H100.png, rt_vs_batch_ap-southeast-T4.png).

Anya: Nice — can you call out the request mix you used? Bursty or steady-state?

Leo: Bursty. Workload: 90% short calls (<=128 tokens), 10% long (512 tokens). Bursts simulated with Poisson arrival (peak lambda ~20 rps per client) for 30s windows, 5m cooldown. We ran across 3 instance families: A100, H100, T4 (FP16 and INT8/GPTQ variants). Kernels: kernel_v2 (fused attention) on H100, kernel_v1 on A100, fallback matmul path on T4.

Sanjay: Which quant levels? Did you test int8?

Leo: Tested FP16 baseline, GPTQ-4bit (per-channel), and qint8 with calibration. Notes: GPTQ gave ~1.6x throughput vs FP16 with small quality delta on eval prompts; INT8 had ~2.0x throughput but some regeneration noise in long-form.

Tess: TL;DR numbers? p50/p95/p99 and sustained throughput per GPU for SSE vs non-streaming?

Leo: Short table (per-GPU single-instance, single-model replica, mixed request mix):
```
us-west / A100 / SSE:    p50=28ms  p95=72ms  p99=210ms  tok/s=920
us-west / A100 / batch:  p50=40ms  p95=110ms p99=400ms  tok/s=2500
eu-central / H100 / SSE: p50=22ms  p95=60ms  p99=180ms  tok/s=1300
eu-central / H100 / batch: p50=35ms  p95=95ms  p99=350ms  tok/s=3500
ap-southeast / T4 / SSE: p50=60ms  p95=180ms p99=600ms  tok/s=280
ap-southeast / T4 / batch:p50=120ms p95=420ms p99=1200ms tok/s=760
```
Notes: "tok/s" measures steady-state token throughput under a sustained mix; SSE latency numbers are end-to-end streaming pX (time to first token for p50, time to full response for p95/p99 when relevant). Batch is non-streaming HTTP endpoint with an adaptive batcher (max_batch=64, batch_timeout=10ms).

Anya: Interesting that SSE has lower p50 but worse p99 in A100 case?

Leo: Right — SSE reduces tail for short responses (first-byte fast because of streaming), but for heavy bursts SSE has CPU/epoll overhead and per-connection state that increases p99 compared to aggressively batched non-streaming which amortizes kernel costs. H100 with kernel_v2 avoids that penalty more effectively, hence better tok/s and lower tails.

Sanjay: Any regional network variance? e.g., us-west -> eu-central RTT impact?

Leo: Yes — we measured pure on-host latency too. Remote RTT adds ~30–70ms depending on region pair. Charts include both raw on-host latency and end-to-end (client->edge->model). Recommendation: for interactive apps prioritize colocated real-time endpoints in region; the extra ~15–40% GPU throughput loss vs batched endpoints is acceptable for UX.

Tess: What about kernel selection guidance?

Leo: Short guidance: H100 + kernel_v2 = best for streaming at scale (keeps p99 down and high tok/s). A100 still fine for cost-sensitive workloads but use larger batch windows for non-streaming. T4: only use for cheap batch inference or embeddings, avoid for low-latency streaming. Quantization: GPTQ-4bit recommended for inference where quality tolerance exists; INT8 for heavy throughput but validate on eval prompts.

infra-bot: perf-deploy/2165 rolled to staging (config: max_batch=64, stream_enabled=true, kernel_hint=auto).

Anya: Any obvious perf regression or weirdness we should track in console?

Leo: Two items to track: 1) SSE p99 spikes when connection churn >500/s per node (we saw ephemeral GC-like pauses in the worker process), 2) quantized INT8 long-form failure rate ~0.6% on our eval suite — flagged as quality regression in the eval dashboard. Filed follow-ups: PERF-322 (SSE connection handling), ML-498 (INT8 eval diffs).

Sanjay: For capacity sizing, rough rule-of-thumb from these runs?

Leo: Yes: pick target p95 latency and throughput; example: to hit p95 <100ms for mixed interactive use in eu-central on H100, reserve ~0.8 H100 per 10k active users (assumes 0.2 rps/user bursty mix). For throughput-heavy (batch embeddings), use batch endpoints and assume ~3.0x tokens per GPU vs streaming. We'll add calc scripts in the perf repo.

Tess: Awesome, can you attach the heatmaps? I'll paste them into the eng-ml confluence page.

Leo: Done. Also added a short note: when switching from SSE->batch for a service, ensure client fallback handles chunked responses (we saw a client that timed out at 250ms and retried, doubling load).

Anya: Thanks — this is actionable. Can we get a condensed one-pager for PMs with the 3 deployment patterns and recommended stacks?

Leo: On it — will drop a short summary by EOD. :thumbsup:
